All ten, because they share one TCP connection
writing.exampleCaption: Same request, three different blocking stories underneath.
writing.explanation: HTTP/1.1 sends one request at a time per connection, so browsers opened six. HTTP/2 multiplexes streams over one TCP connection, which removes application-level blocking but not TCP's — one lost packet still stalls every stream. HTTP/3 moves onto QUIC over UDP, so a lost packet stalls only its own stream, and the handshake folds into TLS.
writing.feedback: TCP must deliver in order, so the whole connection waits.
